Class Tactic

java.lang.Object
dev.swordai.core.rl.Tactic
public final class Tactic extends Object
How it fights for the next half second: the choice the tactics model (TacticNet) makes, and what each choice turns on. Since 21 October, at the user's suggestion: a model of its own whose one job is to choose the way to fight, its choice handed to the acting network as an input.

Up to then the three rules here were on or off for every fight by the config, and each was measured over all opponents at once. The crit back (JumpIn.COUNTER) took the jump-crit chaser from -126 to -38 damage a minute in its first half hour of training and the timer from +133 to +102; holding at the edge (EdgeHold) and stepping back after a hit (StepBack) are right against some opponents and wrong against others in the same way. A choice made per opponent and per moment can keep each where it pays. In the language of hierarchical reinforcement learning this is a manager choosing among options at its own pace (the options framework, Sutton, Precup and Singh 1999; Option-Critic, Bacon et al. AAAI 2017; FeUdal Networks, Vezhnevets et al. ICML 2017), each option here being one of these rule sets with the acting network told which.
